### `call accept`

Answer an incoming call (signalling only), or just mark it received.

Accepting without an audio engine leaves a silent call — useful for automation and testing, useless for talking.

```
tlgr call accept <CALL> [OPTIONS]
```

**mutating · returns `Call`**

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CALL` | text | yes | Call id, or id:access_hash. |

| Flag | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--ack-only` | flag |  | Only mark the call received (busy-lock), do not answer. |
| `--no-ack` | flag |  | Skip the implicit receivedCall so several calls may ring. |

```console
$ tlgr call accept 4815162342 --json
```

### `call get`

State of a call, including the key verification indices.

`conference_supported` says whether `call invite` may be offered at all; `fingerprint` is null unless this session ran the key exchange.

```
tlgr call get <CALL> [OPTIONS]
```

**returns `Call`**

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CALL` | text | yes | Call id, or id:access_hash. |

| Flag | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--fingerprint/--no-fingerprint` | flag | `True` | Derive the key verification indices. |

```console
$ tlgr call get 4815162342 --json
```

<details><summary>Catalog coverage (1 full, 1 partial)</summary>

Full: `calls.conference-supported-flag`

Partial: `calls.emoji-fingerprint`

the four verification values are reported as indices into Telegram's 333-emoji table; tlgr does not bundle the table, and guessing it for a security check would be worse than not printing it


| `USER` | user | any number | Who to add. |

### `call log list`

The Calls tab: every voice, video, group and conference call.

Rows are service messages, decoded here: `messageActionPhoneCall` and `messageActionConferenceCall` become one flat shape.

```
tlgr call log list [OPTIONS]
```

**paginated (`SEARCH` cursor) · returns `Page[CallLogEntry]`**

| Flag | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--missed` | flag |  | Missed calls only (the server filter). |
| `--since` | datetime |  | Lower date bound. |
| `--until` | datetime |  | Upper date bound. |
| `--video` | flag |  | Video calls only (filtered locally). |
| `--with` | user |  | Only calls with this peer. |

Pagination is transport-level: `--limit/-n`, `--cursor TOKEN`, `--all` (walked inside the daemon, paced by the account's own rate limiter).

```console
$ tlgr call log list --json
```

### `call signal`

Relay a tgcalls signalling packet to the peer (bridge plumbing).

The packets are opaque to tlgr. This is also the only route for turning a camera on mid-call: MTProto has no verb for it, only a media-state packet a real engine produces.

```
tlgr call signal <CALL> [OPTIONS]
```

**mutating · returns `Page[CallSignal]`**

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CALL` | text | yes | Call id, or id:access_hash. |

| Flag | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--data` | text |  | Opaque packet to send, base64. |
| `--file` | path |  | Read the packet from a file. |
| `--follow` | flag |  | Keep streaming inbound signalling packets. |
| `--idle-timeout` | duration | `3600` | Give up after silence. |

```console
$ tlgr call signal 4815162342 --data AA== --json
```

### `call start`

Ring a user, voice or video — signalling only, no audio.

tlgr runs the real key exchange and reports the relay list a media engine would use, but it has no media engine: `media` is always `none` and the callee hears silence. `--auto-discard` exists so automation cannot leave a call ringing forever.

```
tlgr call start [USER] [OPTIONS]
```

**mutating · returns `Call`**

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `USER` | user | no | Who to ring. |

| Flag | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--auto-discard` | duration | `60` | Hang up automatically after this long; 0 leaves the call ringing. |
| `--check` | flag |  | Only report whether the peer can be called. Nothing rings. |
| `--from-message` | text |  | Redial the peer of a call log row, or a shared contact card. |
| `--video` | flag |  | Ring as a video call. |
| `--wait` | flag |  | Block until the call is answered or discarded. |
| `--wait-timeout` | duration | `60` | Cap on --wait. |

```console
$ tlgr call start @alice --json
```

### `call watch`

Stream call signalling: incoming rings, state changes, conference invitations.

`should_ring` is resolved here from the app-config and the action flags, so every notifier does not have to get it right separately.

```
tlgr call watch [OPTIONS]
```

**returns `Page[CallEvent]`**

| Flag | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--auto-ack` | flag |  | Send receivedCall for each incoming call (busy-lock). |
| `--conference/--no-conference` | flag | `True` | Also emit conference invitations. |
| `--idle-timeout` | duration | `3600` | Give up after silence. |

```console
$ tlgr call watch --json
```
